programs.title: Foodwise：Qingdao
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Qingdao, China's beer mecca by the sea. With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more.

programs.title: A Vibe of the Village: The Beat of Xiangxi Drums
programs.desc: Experience the vibrant power of Xiangxi Drum Dance. This program delves into the heart of Tujia and Miao cultures, showcasing the rhythmic beats and spirited performances that have echoed through West Hunan's mountains for centuries. Discover the stories, traditions, and raw energy of this captivating folk art.

programs.title: Young dancer of Batang melody
programs.desc: Tibetan girl Tashi Badro from Batang, Ganzi, Sichuan has learned how to do the Xianzi dance both from her mom and a school program. Batang Xianzi is a unique folk dance of the Tibetan ethnic group with a history spanning over 1,000 years on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. In order to keep the Tibetan tradition alive, Badro’s school has offered the dance as a cultural activity. Badro said dancing with her classmates is the happiest moment of her day. Watch the graceful movements of Badro and her peers performing the Xianzi dance.

programs.title: China Bound：Suzhou
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programs.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programs.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of \"lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets.

programs.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programs.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.
